_doc: The address book for dated lake-shore states. Terrain epochs select a shoreline by id; they never silently reuse another epoch's line. STATUS is one of three words and they are not interchangeable: `planned` means geometry is null and the state cannot render until its owning ticket supplies a trace; `traced` means the state has its OWN sourced geometry but no ground has been generated from it yet; `active` means the epoch that addresses it is the one the scene renders. An observation from the wrong date may bound a state, but it may not become that state's adopted line. Where independent readings differ, the full spread is named - as a polygon band where neither reading dominates (1835), or as a run of bank with the tier-1 reading adopted and the tier-2 one recorded beside it (1812). Nothing is ever averaged.

states.label: 15 August 1812 - natural river mouth and pre-harbor shore

bounding_lines.note: Not this state's line. The 1834 epoch's own note says fresh sand is accreting north of the north pier, so Wright's lake shore there lies ON or EAST of where the 1812 shore ran. It bounds the 1812 shore from the east and is recorded here rather than copied into the 1812 file, which is what keeps the two states from aliasing.

states.note: Supplied by T-1242, the first piece of T-0468. There is no survey of the pre-cut mouth, so this state is DERIVED in the open rather than traced: Wright's 1834 reading of the same landform is the base planform, the drafted piers and the shore accreting behind them are dropped, the bar is declared continuous to the mainland with the isthmus itself left unmodelled, and the mouth is set at the half mile below the fort that Lt. Swearingen walked and wrote down in 1803. The compilation's 'near present Madison Street' is 94.9 m further south and is kept as the alternative, not averaged in. Wright's own 1834 bar tip falls 9.2 m south of the adopted station - an 1803 distance on foot and an 1834 survey agreeing to within ten metres. NO ELEVATION IS CLAIMED: the ground this planform implies is T-1243.

states.label: 1 July 1835 — harbor cut and eroding south shore
states.note: Wright's 1834 line is the scene's primary reading where it exists. Rees & Rucker's 1849 line is fourteen years late and is only a lower bound below Twelfth Street: the 1835 water's edge stood on it or east of it. The two fitted sheets overlap from local N -1300 to -2000 and differ at every 100 m station. Their full spread is the named band; no midpoint or smoothed compromise is adopted.

states.label: 1 July 1904 — Lake Michigan's edge beside the Illinois Central, Prairie Avenue
states.address_date_basis: the owner's ruling of 2026-09-26, with Glessner House: the Prairie Avenue model is centred on 1904, and its scene defaults to 1 July (the project's day-of-year convention, as 1835-07-01).

address_date_superseded.why: T-1249 derived 1 July 1888 for the 1880s framing this state was reserved under. The owner's ruling of 2026-09-26 moved the Prairie Avenue scene to 1904 and said the 1888 records may stay; they do, and the 1880s date still resolves to this state through e1871_postfire, but the line this state carries is the one a 1904 scene stands on and nothing here is dated 1888.

dated_lines.note: Seven years after the scene: the 1904 edge stood on it or west of it, on the one inference that a built edge beside the railway moves only lakeward unless something is removed, and nothing records a removal.
Eighteen years before the scene: the 1904 edge stood on it or east of it.

scene_line.note: The one waterline a scene has to render. Neither sheet is of 1904, so neither becomes this state's line: the scene line is reconstructed inside the band they bound, on its eastern (1911) bound where a 1911 sheet draws the edge, and on the 1886 planform moved east by the measured offsets where none does. Past the last sheet (segment F) it is carried on a bearing and nothing bounds it.

states.note: Supplied by T-1250. Two sheets bracket 1904 and neither is it: Sanborn 1911 (sheets 20 and 28) inks the water's edge beside the Illinois Central in two short runs, and Robinson 1886 (plate 10) draws it from above 16th Street to 18th. Where both draw it the 1911 edge stands EAST of the 1886 one — 14.0-18.7 m (mean 17.0) at the 16th Street run and 17.8-21.2 m (mean 19.9) at the 18th — which the two fits' few metres of uncertainty cannot explain: the right-of-way widened into the lake between them. Both sheets are therefore BOUNDS, 1886 from before and 1911 from after, and the spread between them is the named band, not a midpoint. The scene still needs one waterline, so `scene_line` is one, reconstructed (L287) on the band's eastern bound - the nearer date, and Glessner House reads everything on these sheets but two houses as standing in 1904 - with six segments saying which stretch stands on the traced 1911 edge, which on the 1886 planform moved by measured offsets, and which (F, south of where sheet 28's easternmost track leaves the paper) on a bearing alone. It is deliberately not an alias of either earlier state, and tools/check_shoreline_states.py compares coordinates to prove it.
